utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Judge Antonetti, could you put your -- please turn your microphone on, please.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Case number IT-97-25/1-PT, the Prosecutor versus Mitar Rasevic.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Microphone, please, for the Presiding Judge.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. Rasevic, can you hear the interpreter? So I shall ask the Prosecution to introduce itself, please.

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: Good afternoon, Your Honour. For the Prosecution appear Ms. Diane Boles, the case manager, Bill Smith, and my name is Hildegard Uertz-Retzlaff.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you very much. I would now like the Defence to stand up and introduce himself.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE DOMAZET
utterances.text: [Interpretation] My name is Vladimir Domazet, I'm the lead counsel for Mr. Rasevic.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you very much. I would like to welcome all the people present in this room. The Prosecution and the Defence as well as the accused, Mr. Rasevic, who is present in this courtroom. This hearing is being held pursuant to the holding of a Status Conference as are mentioned in the Rules of Procedure and Evidence, and Article -- Rule -- according to Rule 65 bis, the Pre-Trial Judge must convene a pre-trial hearing 120 days after the initial appearance. This was a view to exchanging information between the parties and making sure that one can organise a fair and expeditious trial and also examine the status report of the hearing and also enable the accused to raise a number of questions relating to the mental and physical condition of the accused. Since the initial appearance, there was a problem relating to the Defence counsel of Mr. Rasevic. Since then, Mr. Domazet has been assigned by the Registrar. There remains no pending questions thereof, I believe.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE DOMAZET
utterances.text: [Interpretation] No.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: I must also look into a preliminary motions on the 20th of November, 2003. The Defence filed a preliminary motion with a view to challenging the indictment. Since that day, the Prosecutor seized the Chamber and filed a motion dated 2nd of December and asked leave to amend the indictment. It would be appropriate, therefore, that the Defence respond to this motion before the 15th of December, 2003, and provide the response to the motion filed by the Prosecution. And in the event the Defence has preliminary motions, to state in response to this motion, this should be filed before the 14th of January, 2003. The Chamber will then render its decision, which will relate on the -- relate to the preliminary motion of the 20th of November, 2003, and will also relate to the motion dated 2nd of December, 2003, and pertaining to the amendment of the indictment. The Chamber will then render its decision in the course of the month of January. In addition, I need to ask the Prosecution to let the Chamber know about the status of the disclosure of supporting material pursuant to Article -- to Rule 66. So, Madam Prosecutor, how do we stand vis-a-vis disclosing of material and Rule 66 of the Rules of Procedure and Evidence, please?

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: Your Honour, the supporting material has been disclosed to the accused on the 21st of October. So it's -- we were within the 30 days that were required.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you very much. Mr. Domazet, since the 21st of October, you have had all the supporting material made available to you pursuant to Article 66. Do you have any further difficulties?

utterances.speaker: MR. DOMAZET
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I believe there are no further questions. The accused received the documents himself. I have reviewed all the supporting material, and I think there are no problems relating to this.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Regarding disclosure pursuant to Rule 68 of the Rules of Procedure and Evidence, any exculpatory material that might be disclosed. Could the Prosecution please tell us how they stand vis-a-vis this particular point.

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: Your Honour, part of the supporting material actually already included a lot of Rule 68 materials because we had filed almost every statement that dealt with the KP Dom and in particular the accused, and it includes also Rule 68 material. In addition, we -- we intend to have consultations with Defence counsel in the very near future, and after these consultations, we will then have a better overview what could be potential Rule 68 materials. Of course, we'll do the usual checks on the database, but these consultations would enable us to be more specific.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you very much. Mr. Domazet, the Prosecution has just told us that Rule 68 material have already been made available to you and disclosed to the accused on the 21st of October. The Prosecution is, therefore, checking to see whether there is any additional material to disclose. Do you have any comments to make in this regard?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE DOMAZET
utterances.text: [Interpretation] No, Judge Antonetti, I don't have any comments. I understand the position of the Prosecution full well, and for the time being there are no problems.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you very much. Pursuant to Rule 65 bis, I must ask the accused whether he has any health problems. Could you stand up, please, and can you tell me if you have any health problems or if you are fit and well?

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, I have no problems, neither as far as my physical health is concerned, neither as far as my mental health is concerned.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Fine. As far as your conditions in the detention centre are concerned?

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] As far as the detention conditions are concerned, there are no problems.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you. You may sit down. Does the Prosecution or the Defence have any other question to submit today? Madam Prosecutor.

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: No, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you. I shall now turn to the Defence.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE DOMAZET
utterances.text: [Interpretation] No, there are no further questions.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] This, therefore, ends this Status Conference pursuant to the pre-trial phase of any proceeding. There will be another Status Conference held in four months' time, within the 120-day time frame. We will have made a lot of progress. Decision will be rendered in the month of December pertaining on the one hand to the filing for leave to amend the indictment by the Prosecution and pertaining also to the Defence's preliminary motion, and we hope that this phase will not last forever and too long. I would therefore kindly recommend that the two parties get together and that we expedite this proceeding. As you know, we have the duty to conduct expeditious trials, and this is in the interest of the accused as you well know. As there are no further questions, I wish to adjourn this hearing for today. Thank you.

procedural_notes.text: ---  Whereupon the Status Conference adjourned at
